newsitem.title: UK: UK insolvencies fall slightly in 1996 - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: UK insolvencies fall slightly in 1996 - KPMG.

text.p: The number of bankruptcies and liquidations in Britain fell in 1996, but the rate of decrease is slowing, KPMG Corporate Recovery said on Thursday.
KPMG said there were 21,803 bankruptcies during 1996, 0.6 percent lower than in 1995. Total liquidations fell 4.9 percent in the same period.
The 1996 figures were the lowest since 1990, indicating that economic conditions continue to improve.
"I am encouraged that the number of liquidations and bankruptcies continues to fall, albeit by a relatively small amount," said Mike Wheeler, head of KPMG Corporate Recovery.
He said he expected the number to decline further in 1997, but added that no matter what the state of the economy, there would always be businesses which fail.
All but two regions saw a small reduction in liquidations, it said. The north east and south west of England both suffered moderate increases.
